title: Failure Cascade Synthesizer for Soft-State Loss and Rate/Capacity Probes
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Purpose: Build a reusable test harness (Failure Cascade Synthesizer) that composes small, deterministic failure primitives to emulate realistic production cascades that hurt soft state, capacity signals, and routing decisions.

Motivation: Existing chaos runs cover whole-region blackouts and GPU pool depletion in isolation. We need a tool that composes thinner, asymmetric failures that reveal problems in graceful degradation: stale prefix cache rehydration, misrouted traffic when regions exhibit slow signals, circuit breakers tripping too late/early, and load-shedding that amplifies downstream latency. The goal is to exercise multi-step cascades that happen in the wild (e.g., slow dependency leading to queue buildup, leading to admission-control misclassification, leading to regional failover and amplification).

Deliverables:
- A harness that sequences primitives (latency bump, connection drop, token-level KV cache loss, quota signal delay, GPU scheduler starvation) and exposes a DSL for composing scenarios.
- A canon set of 8 scenarios that cover asymmetric region latency, partial KV/cache corruption, transient scheduler preemption, and dependency signal-silence.
- Automated injection jobs runnable in staging and a guarded run in canary production with observability hooks and automatic rollback triggers.

Scope boundaries: No changes to runtime production admission control or SLO targets as part of the experiment. The harness should run using feature-flagged test endpoints and non-customer traffic. Any test that affects global capacity must be approved by capacity on-call and ops leads.
success_criteria: Harness can express and run 8 canonical scenarios end-to-end in staging within CI under 45 minutes
Identify at least 3 concrete failure modes that cause >5% increased P99 latency or >3x retry amplification under controlled runs
Produce a set of graduated mitigations (circuit breaker tuning, admission-control heuristics, KV cache rehydration backoff) that reduce observed regressions by >=50% in follow-up runs
Integrate automated detection: alert rule + dashboard tile for the specific signal patterns produced by the scenarios
test_scenarios: Asymmetric Region Slowdown: Inject sustained +200ms tail latency for Region-B dependencies while Region-A remains healthy to expose routing and diversion oscillations
Stale-Prefix Rehydration: Simulate loss of KV cache for 10% of requests followed by burst traffic to observe tokenized regen storms
Scheduler Drift: Thin GPU preemption windows (50ms) across a subset of instances to create intermittent capacity degradation and request retransmission waves
Circuit Oscillation: Flip intentionally noisy dependency health checks to exercise circuit opener/breaker hysteresis and observe retry fan-out
Quota Signal Delay: Delay quota/usage signals to the admission controller to test optimistic acceptance then sudden shed behavior
Silent Dependency Fails: Drop RPC responses without error to emulate a silent stall and catch clients that assume success on timeouts
Cross-Region Chase: Force stepwise region ejection and reintroduction with small overlaps to verify sticky-routing and state reconciliation
Mixed Failure Composition: Combine a small KV loss with quota delay and a 20% GPU pool soft-exhaustion to trigger multi-tier degradation
metrics: Per-region P50/P95/P99 latency for generation endpoints
Request retry amplification (ratio of retries to originals) per minute
Admission-control accept vs shed rates and reasons
KV cache hit/miss and rehydration rates and associated CPU/GPU spin
Model-level tokens/sec and queue depth for GPU pools
Error budget burn rate and simulated SLO breach windows
notes_updates: 2026-03-02: Triage meeting. Agreed P1. Scope refined to staging-first with one guarded prod run. Ops and capacity leads added as approvers.
2026-03-05: PoC DSL sketched (sequence primitives + timebox). Eng infra to provide injection hooks for scheduler and KV layer.
2026-03-08: Discovered admission-controller lacks labeled reason codes; added to deps so shed telemetry can be attributed. Created ENG-14310 to add reason_codes to AC logs.
2026-03-11: Ran preliminary staging scenario 1. Observed unexpected rehydration storm that doubled API CPU for 3s — captured traces and flamegraphs under drive link.

2026-03-14: Design review with runtime and console teams. Console will add an ephemeral tile to surface scenario-specific metrics during runs. Planning two follow-up mitigations: circuit hysteresis tuning (low) and staged rehydration backoff (medium).
implementation_plan: Week 1: Build DSL + primitive adapters (latency, drop, quota-delay, kv-reset, gpu-soft-saturate)
Week 2: Implement the 8 canonical scenarios and CI job for staging runs
Week 3: Run staging matrix, collect metrics, write runbook sections, and propose mitigations
Week 4: Guarded canary run in prod with ops oversight and automated rollback triggers
